deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is German prose lecture notes on ancient history, continuing 'B. Geschichte von Athen' from the previous folio. The hand and the content suggest a student's notebook of history lectures; nothing indicates Gauss's own mathematical work. The content, in order:

(1) Menestheus reigned during the Trojan War, continuing the king list from the previous page.

(2) The last king was Codrus. Around his time came the Ionian migration. He died c. 1068 BC.

(3) After him the Athenians chose no more kings. Instead there were archons taken from the family of Codrus, beginning with his son Medon and ending with Alcmaeon. These archons held office hereditarily and for life, but were accountable for their rule. Thirteen of them ruled from 1068 to 752. The most important event of this period was the Ionian migration to Asia Minor.

(4) Next came a class of archons holding office for 10 years. Seven of them followed one another, 752 to 682.

(5) This too was abolished. Archons were then chosen every year, and a college of (nine) archons was founded to introduce a more republican constitution. Even so, this did not secure much freedom for the nation.

(6) From 682 to 592 a family aristocracy arose, as the nobles pushed their way into the first archonships.

(7) A written law code was felt to be needed. The task was given to the archon Draco in 622. His laws were too severe and so were not observed for long.

(8) Solon was more fortunate and laid the foundation of the city's later greatness. He became archon in 592. His legislation is compared with Lycurgus's; the exact phrase is uncertain, probably 'more perfect than'. He divided the people by wealth into four classes:
- I. the rich;
- II. knights (Ritter);
- III. middling citizens;
- IV. the poor.

(9) The property qualifications are given as annual yields from land: 500 medimni for the rich, 400 for the knights, 300 for the middle class, and less than 300 for the poor.

The only 'computations' implicit in the page are chronological differences:
- 752 − 682 = 70 = 7 × 10 years for the seven decennial archons, which is consistent.
- 1068 − 752 = 316 years for 13 life archons, about 24.3 years each.
errors: Solon's census figures are historically misstated. The standard tradition (Aristotle, Ath. Pol. 7; Plutarch, Solon 18) gives pentakosiomedimnoi ≥500 medimni, hippeis ≥300, zeugitai ≥200, and thetes below 200. The notes give 500/400/300/<300.
The dates for Draco (622) and Solon's archonship (592) are slightly off from the now-usual 621/620 and 594/593 BC. They are consistent with some older chronologies, so this is not a clear error.
Not an error by the author: the machine transcription's '168 — 752' should read '1068 — 752', in line with 'c. 1068' earlier on the page.

results.what: Lecture notes on early Athenian constitutional history: kings, life archons, decennial archons, annual archons, Draco, and Solon's timocratic classes.
results.modern_name: Standard textbook narrative of the archaic Athenian constitution (Ath. Pol./Plutarch tradition)
results.usually_credited_to: Ancient sources (Aristotle's Athenaion Politeia, Plutarch); 18th/19th-c. German school history textbooks

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics. It is routine history-lecture notes, probably not even in Gauss's hand, reproducing the standard school narrative of early Athens.

checkable.asserts: The seven decennial archons fill exactly the stated interval 752–682 BC.
The average tenure of the 13 life archons over 1068–752 BC is 316/13 ≈ 24.3 years.
The 'family aristocracy' period runs 90 years, up to Solon's archonship.
In the notes' chronology, Draco's code precedes Solon's archonship by 30 years.

transcription_corrections: 'wurde ein Kollegium von neun [?] gestiftet' is probably 'ein Kollegium von [neun] Personen gestiftet, um mehr eine republ[ikanische] Verfassung einzuführen'; the duplicated 'Vorkehrung einzuführen' is a misreading.
'zu den ersten Stellen der Archonten verdrängten' is probably 'zu den ersten Stellen der Archonten drängten'.
'Seine Gesetzgebung wurde wertvoll [?] war aber als die von Lycurg' is probably 'Seine Gesetzgebung war weit vollkommener als die von Lycurg' or similar. It is a comparison, not 'wertvoll'.
'III mittel [?] ... Bürger' is likely 'III mittelmäßige Bürger'.
'Glücklicher war [-Lycurg-] {+Sie+} Solon': the inserted word above the line is uncertain and probably not 'Sie'; the main reading 'Glücklicher war Solon' stands.
'Dem Sohn Medon, der letzte Alkmaeon' should read 'Der erste [war] sein Sohn Medon, der letzte Alkmaeon'.
